numerical_failure.expected_behavior: pd.to_datetime should produce identical UTC timestamps for the same calendar values when the input DataFrame columns ['year','month','day','hour','minute','second'] are provided as float64 vs float32; i.e., for the same df values, the outputs must satisfy ts.equals(ts64) and ts.equals(ts32) where ts = pd.to_datetime(df, utc=True), ts32 = pd.to_datetime(df.astype('float32'), utc=True), and ts64 = pd.to_datetime(df.astype('float64'), utc=True).
trigger_conditions: Calling pd.to_datetime on a DataFrame with columns ['year','month','day','hour','minute','second'] where the DataFrame is cast to float32 (df.astype('float32')) leads to a float32 precision discrepancy relative to float64.
Calling pd.to_datetime on the same DataFrame cast to float64 (df.astype('float64')) should not have the discrepancy; after the fix, float inputs are cast to float64 in coerce(values).

oracle_clues: Issue commentary: "Seems like a float32 precision issue." (issue#60506).

Fix approach: in pandas/core/tools/datetimes.py, coerce(values) casts float inputs to float64: "if is_float_dtype(values.dtype): values = values.astype(\"float64\")" with comment "prevent prevision issues in case of float32 # GH#60506".

Issue reproducer defines ts = pd.to_datetime(df, utc=True), ts32 = pd.to_datetime(df.astype('float32'), utc=True), ts64 = pd.to_datetime(df.astype('float64'), utc=True), and checks correctness using assertions: assert ts.equals(ts64) and assert ts.equals(ts32).

category_specific_evidence: Issue/annotation: “Seems like a float32 precision issue.” (issue#60506)
PR: “Fix float32 precision issues in pd.to_datetime”. (PR#60510 / commit)

Reproduction snippet uses three dtype regimes: `ts = pd.to_datetime(df, utc=True)`, `ts32 = pd.to_datetime(df.astype('float32'), utc=True)`, `ts64 = pd.to_datetime(df.astype('float64'), utc=True)` and then asserts `ts.equals(ts64)` and `ts.equals(ts32)` (issue#60506)

Test added for float32: `result = to_datetime(df.astype(np.float32), cache=cache)` with `expected = Series([Timestamp("20150204 06:58:10.001002003"), Timestamp("20160305 07:59:11.001002003")])` followed by `tm.assert_series_equal(result, expected)` (test_diff in pandas/tests/tools/test_to_datetime.py)

Fix implemented by coercing float inputs to float64: in `coerce(values)`, `if is_float_dtype(values.dtype): values = values.astype("float64")` with comment “prevent prevision issues in case of float32 # GH#60506” (diff in pandas/core/tools/datetimes.py)
